paragraphs: Here's what I want you to take home, friend. Solomon had finished the temple, the palace, everything he wanted to do, and God still showed up with a word for him. He opened with “I have heard your prayer and petition before Me.” Finishing the big project is not the end of walking with God, and God keeps talking after the ribbon is cut (1 Kings 9:1-3).

Then comes the smallest word with the BIGGEST weight: IF. God promised to put His Name in the temple forever, and He also told Solomon to walk before Him as his father David walked, “with a heart of integrity and uprightness” (1 Kings 9:3-4). God's promise stands, and He still asked for a heart that stays turned toward Him. The other side of that IF was heavy, friend: if Solomon or his sons turned away to serve other gods, God said the land and the temple would be lost (1 Kings 9:6-7).

So what does it mean for you? A good start, a beautiful building or a big finish won't keep your heart pointed at God for you. The people passing the rubble got their answer: they had forsaken the LORD their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt (1 Kings 9:9). Stay close to the One who has already carried you and keep your heart His, because the story isn't over, and there's more to come.
